The test image shows cut corn stalks with **black nodes**, dark discoloration on the stalk exterior, and what appears to be broken/snapped stalks at node areas. The nodes are distinctly blackened with yellow-tan coloration on the internodes.

Let me check the part index and then view reference images for the top candidates.

This is a stem image. Top stem candidates with black nodes/dark discoloration: Physoderma_Stalk_Rot, Anthracnose_Leaf_Spot_And_Top_Dieback, Charcoal_Stalk_Rot, Diplodia_Stalk_Rot.

Viewing references one at a time, starting with Physoderma_Stalk_Rot (black nodes match best):
This Physoderma_Stalk_Rot reference shows scattered black dots on green stalk - doesn't match the test's black nodes on broken stalks. Let me check Anthracnose next.
This Anthracnose reference shows shiny black areas on stalk rind and rotted nodes - closer to test image. Let me check Charcoal_Stalk_Rot next.
Charcoal_Stalk_Rot shows shredded pith with dark interior - not matching the test's black exterior nodes. Let me check Diplodia_Stalk_Rot.
Diplodia_Stalk_Rot shows tan/brown broken stalk - much lighter than the test's black discoloration. Let me check the second Anthracnose stem reference.

This is an almost perfect match to the test image - same wooden surface background, same black/yellow-tan mottled stalk exterior, same appearance. Strongly indicates **Anthracnose_Leaf_Spot_And_Top_Dieback**.

Let me view 3 more from different classes to complete my budget of 8.
Purple_Leaf_Sheath shows green stalks with discrete dark spots - does not match. Let me check Charcoal_Stalk_Rot second image and Diplodia_Stalk_Rot second image.
Charcoal_Stalk_Rot shows shredded stalks with stringy strands - doesn't match. One more view needed.

Diplodia_Stalk_Rot shows light tan/cream stalk with small black pycnidia - completely different from the test image's heavily blackened stalk rind.

**Summary of evidence:**
- Test image: multiple corn stalks on wooden surface with gravel background, showing extensive black/dark discoloration mottled with yellow-tan on the stalk exterior, broken/snapped at nodes
- `Anthracnose_Leaf_Spot_And_Top_Dieback/stem/Corn_Disease_60.jpg` is an almost identical match - same wooden/gravel background, same black-yellow-tan mottled rind appearance, same stalk presentation
- All other candidates (Charcoal, Diplodia, Physoderma, Purple_Leaf_Sheath) look clearly different
